tldr: BattleAgentBench is a fine-grained benchmark for evaluating LLMs' cooperation and competition capabilities in multi-agent systems, featuring three difficulty levels and seven stages across single-agent, paired-agent, and multi-agent scenarios.
contributions: Introduction of BattleAgentBench, a fine-grained multi-agent cooperation and competition evaluation benchmark with three levels (single-agent to multi-agent)
Design of seven stages from easy to difficult assessing basic single-agent abilities, cooperative abilities, and competitive abilities
Thorough evaluation of 11 LLMs (4 API-based and 7 open-source models)
methods: The authors designed a benchmark using a turn-based game called Battle City, modeled as a Markov Decision Process. The benchmark includes three difficulty levels: Level 1 (single-agent navigation), Level 2 (paired-agent cooperation and competition), and Level 3 (multi-agent static, dynamic, and hybrid cooperation-competition). Eleven LLMs were evaluated—four API-based and seven open-source—with metrics including Forward Distance, Format Accuracy, Move Accuracy, and Score. An ablation study removed the cooperation interface to isolate collaborative ability effects.
results: API-based models significantly outperformed open-source small models on Level 1, with claude3.5-sonnet and gpt-4o-mini effectively completing navigation tasks while open-source models had goal completion rates below 50%. On Level 2, only claude3.5-sonnet and gpt-4o-mini achieved relatively high scores. On Level 3, these two models again led, with claude3.5-sonnet uniquely maintaining high movement accuracy. The ablation study showed that only claude3.5-sonnet and gpt-4o-mini benefited from cooperation, while other models' scores increased when cooperation was removed. However, even top models showed only modest improvement from cooperation.
limitations: Open-source small models perform poorly even on simple tasks. Even top API-based models show only modest improvement from cooperation and have significant room for improvement on complex collaborative and competitive tasks. The gap between models narrows on difficult tasks, suggesting current LLMs struggle with nuanced multi-agent dynamics.
